sanskrit: śruṣṭī vāṁ yajña udyataḥ sajoṣā manuṣvad vṛktabarhiṣo yajadhyai | ā ya indrāvaruṇāv iṣe adya mahe sumnāya maha āvavartat ||
english: Your joint hearing rises with this sacrifice, O Indra-Varuṇa, when the kusa-strewn altar is ready for worship in the manner of Manu; he who turns to you today for sustenance, for great favour, for great bounty — may he obtain it.

sanskrit: tā hi śreṣṭhā devatātā tujā śūrāṇāṁ śaviṣṭhā tā hi bhūtam | maghonām maṁhiṣṭhā tuviśuṣma ṛtena vṛtraturā sarvasenā ||
english: For you two are the best among the gods, impetuous, the mightiest of heroes, the most powerful — thus have you been; most liberal to the generous, O you of mighty vigour, vanquishers of Vṛtra by holy order, with your entire host.

sanskrit: tā gṛṇīhi namasyebhiḥ śūṣaiḥ sumnebhir indrāvaruṇā cakānā | vajreṇānyaḥ śavasā hanti vṛtraṁ siṣakty anyo vṛjaneṣu vipraḥ ||
english: Praise them both, O Indra-Varuṇa, delighting, with reverent powers and with eulogies of goodwill; one smites Vṛtra with the vajra by his might, the other, the sage, attends upon the settlement of men.

sanskrit: gnāś ca yan naraś ca vāvṛdhanta viśve devāso narāṁ svagūrtāḥ | praibhya indrāvaruṇā mahitvā dyauś ca pṛthivi bhūtam urvī ||
english: When the goddesses and the men grew strong, all the gods delighting in the praise of men — from them, O Indra-Varuṇa, in your greatness you arose; O Heaven and Earth, you both became the wide ones.

sanskrit: sa it sudānuḥ svavām̐ ṛtāvendrā yo vāṁ varuṇa dāśati tman | iṣā sa dviṣas tared dāsvān vaṁsad rayiṁ rayivataś ca janān ||
english: He truly is the good giver, the bounteous, the upright, O Indra, who devotes himself to you two, O Varuṇa; with nourishment shall the pious one overcome his enemies, shall win wealth and men abounding in riches.

sanskrit: yaṁ yuvaṁ dāśvadhvarāya devā rayiṁ dhattho vasumantam purukṣum | asme sa indrāvaruṇāv api ṣyāt pra yo bhānakti vanuṣām aśastīḥ ||
english: That wealth, full of goods, full of abundance, which you two, O gods, bestow on the worshipper who performs sacrifice — may that be ours, O Indra-Varuṇa, he who shatters the curses of his foes.

sanskrit: uta naḥ sutrātro devagopāḥ sūribhya indrāvaruṇā rayiḥ ṣyāt | yeṣāṁ śuṣmaḥ pṛtanāsu sāhvān pra sadyo dyumnā tirate taturiḥ ||
english: And may wealth come to us — your well-guarded worshippers, O Indra-Varuṇa, protected by the gods — to whom the vigour that overcomes in battles, the fame, swiftly spreads, the far-reaching one.

sanskrit: nū na indrāvaruṇā gṛṇānā pṛṅktaṁ rayiṁ sauśravasāya devā | itthā gṛṇanto mahinasya śardho 'po na nāvā duritā tarema ||
english: Now, O Indra-Varuṇa, being praised, yoke riches for us, O gods, unto great fame; even thus praising the host of the mighty one, may we cross all adversities as a boat crosses water.

sanskrit: pra samrāje bṛhate manma nu priyam arca devāya varuṇāya saprathaḥ | ayaṁ ya urvī mahinā mahivrataḥ kratvā vibhāty ajaro na śociṣā ||
english: Sing now a beloved song, wide-resounding, to the great sovereign, to the divine Varuṇa; he who, vast in his greatness, of mighty ordinance, shines by his wisdom undecaying as with a flame.

sanskrit: indrāvaruṇā sutapāv imaṁ sutaṁ somam pibatam madyaṁ dhṛtavratā | yuvo ratho adhvaraṁ devavītaye prati svasaram upa yāti pītaye ||
english: O Indra-Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed draught, O you of steadfast ordinance, drink this pressed, intoxicating Soma; your chariot comes to the sacrifice day by day for the delight of the gods, for drinking.

sanskrit: indrāvaruṇā madhumattamasya vṛṣṇaḥ somasya vṛṣaṇā vṛṣethām | idaṁ vām andhaḥ pariṣiktam asme āsadyāsmin barhiṣi mādayethām ||
english: O Indra-Varuṇa, both bulls, drink your fill of this most sweetly inebriating, vigour-giving Soma; this drink has been poured out for you two among us — be seated on this sacred grass and rejoice.

sanskrit: saṁ vāṁ karmaṇā sam iṣā hinomīndrāviṣṇū apasas pāre asya | juṣethāṁ yajñaṁ draviṇaṁ ca dhattam ariṣṭair naḥ pathibhiḥ pārayantā ||
english: With prayer and with offering I impel you both together, O Indra-Viṣṇu, to the far end of this work; take pleasure in the sacrifice, bestow riches upon us, and lead us along unharmed paths.

sanskrit: yā viśvāsāṁ janitārā matīnām indrāviṣṇū kalaśā somadhānā | pra vāṁ giraḥ śasyamānā avantu pra stomāso gīyamānāso arkaiḥ ||
english: O Indra-Viṣṇu, begettors of all thoughts, bowls that hold the Soma — may the hymns recited for you two be fruitful, may the praises when sung with chants thrive.

sanskrit: indrāviṣṇū madapatī madānām ā somaṁ yātaṁ draviṇo dadhānā | saṁ vām añjantv aktubhir matīnāṁ saṁ stomāsaḥ śasyamānāsa ukthaiḥ ||
english: O Indra-Viṣṇu, lords of joys, of ecstasies, come to the Soma, bringing treasure; may the devotions anoint you both with their gleams, and the praises with their recitations and hymns.

sanskrit: ā vām aśvāso abhimātiṣāha indrāviṣṇū sadhamādo vahantu | juṣethāṁ viśvā havanā matīnām upa brahmāṇi śṛṇutaṁ giro me ||
english: May horses that overcome the foe carry you both hither, O Indra-Viṣṇu, you who rejoice together; take pleasure in all the invocations of the prayers — hear, O you two, my devotions and my hymns.

sanskrit: indrāviṣṇū tat panayāyyaṁ vāṁ somasya mada uru cakramāthe | akṛṇutam antarikṣaṁ varīyo 'prathataṁ jīvase no rajāṁsi ||
english: O Indra-Viṣṇu, that is worthy of wonder for you both — in the exhilaration of Soma you two have widely stridden; you have made the wide firmament, you have spread out the realms for our living.

sanskrit: indrāviṣṇū haviṣā vāvṛdhānāgrādvānā namasā rātahavyā | ghṛtāsutī draviṇaṁ dhattam asme samudrāḥ sthaḥ kalaśaḥ somadhānaḥ ||
english: O Indra-Viṣṇu, grown mighty with the oblation, who press forward, who receive the offering with reverence — you who pour ghee, bestow wealth upon us; you are the oceans, the bowl that holds the Soma.

sanskrit: indrāviṣṇū pibatam madhvo asya somasya dasrā jaṭharam pṛṇethām | ā vām andhāṁsi madirāṇy agmann upa brahmāṇi śṛṇutaṁ havam me ||
english: O Indra-Viṣṇu, wondrous ones, drink of this sweet Soma and fill your bellies; may the exhilarating draughts come to you both — hear my devotions, hear my call.

sanskrit: ubhā jigyathur na parā jayethe na parā jigye kataraś canainoḥ | indraś ca viṣṇo yad aspṛdhethāṁ tredhā sahasraṁ vi tad airayethām ||
english: Both of you have conquered, neither of you is defeated, neither one of you two has ever been overcome; O Viṣṇu, when you and Indra competed, you two set that thousandfold wealth flying in three directions.

sanskrit: ghṛtavatī bhuvanānām abhiśriyorvī pṛthvī madhudughe supeśasā | dyāvāpṛthivī varuṇasya dharmaṇā viṣkabhite ajare bhūriretasā ||
english: Rich in ghee, the glory of all beings, the wide and broad Heaven and Earth that yield honey, beautiful in form — by Varuṇa's ordinance the two are propped apart, the undecaying ones, rich in seed.

sanskrit: asaścantī bhūridhāre payasvatī ghṛtaṁ duhāte sukṛte śucivrate | rājantī asya bhuvanasya rodasī asme retaḥ siñcataṁ yan manurhitam ||
english: Inexhaustible, flowing with many streams, full of milk, the two world-halves yield ghee to the pious one of pure conduct; the two shining ones, rulers of this world — pour upon us the seed that Manu established.

sanskrit: yo vām ṛjave kramaṇāya rodasī marto dadāśa dhiṣaṇe sa sādhati | pra prajābhir jāyate dharmaṇas pari yuvoḥ siktā viṣurūpāṇi savratā ||
english: The mortal who offers to you two, O Heaven and Earth, O Wisdom-goddesses, for the straight stepping — he prospers; he is born forward among offspring from your ordinance; what has been poured into you two takes many forms, sharing one law.

sanskrit: ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī abhīvṛte ghṛtaśriyā ghṛtapṛcā ghṛtāvṛdhā | urvī pṛthvī hotṛvūrye purohite te id viprā īḻate sumnam iṣṭaye ||
english: Heaven and Earth, encompassed with ghee, glorious with ghee, mixed with ghee, swelling with ghee — the wide, the broad ones, coveted by the Hotar priest, set foremost — them do the sages pray to for favour, for offering.

sanskrit: madhu no dyāvāpṛthivī mimikṣatām madhuścutā madhudughe madhuvrate | dadhāne yajñaṁ draviṇaṁ ca devatā mahi śravo vājam asme suvīryam ||
english: May Heaven and Earth sprinkle sweetness upon us, dripping honey, yielding honey, whose rite is honey; bearing the sacrifice and wealth, the divine ones — may they grant us great fame, food, and heroic strength.

sanskrit: ūrjaṁ no dyauś ca pṛthivī ca pinvatām pitā mātā viśvavidā sudaṁsasā | saṁrarāṇe rodasī viśvaśambhuvā saniṁ vājaṁ rayim asme sam invatām ||
english: May Heaven and Earth, father and mother, all-knowing, of wondrous deeds, swell refreshment upon us; may the two world-halves, well-disposed, bringers of good to all, pour upon us gain, food, and wealth.

sanskrit: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā bāhū ayaṁsta savanāya sukratuḥ | ghṛtena pāṇī abhi pruṣṇute makho yuvā sudakṣo rajaso vidharmaṇi ||
english: The god Savitṛ of wise counsel has stretched up his golden arms for the pressing rite; the vigorous, young, skilled one moistens his hands with ghee, in the holding apart of the firmament.

sanskrit: devasya vayaṁ savituḥ savīmani śreṣṭhe syāma vasunaś ca dāvane | yo viśvasya dvipado yaś catuṣpado niveśane prasave cāsi bhūmanaḥ ||
english: May we be in the stimulation of the god Savitṛ, in the best, in the giving of riches; you who are the abundance of all the two-footed and four-footed — at their settling and at their setting forth.

sanskrit: adabdhebhiḥ savitaḥ pāyubhiṣ ṭvaṁ śivebhir adya pari pāhi no gayam | hiraṇyajihvaḥ suvitāya navyase rakṣā mākin no aghaśaṁsa īśata ||
english: With your undeceived, auspicious guardians, O Savitṛ, protect our home today; O golden-tongued one, for a new happy fortune — guard us so that no evil-speaker may have power over us.

sanskrit: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā damūnā hiraṇyapāṇiḥ pratidoṣam asthāt | ayohanur yajato mandrajihva ā dāśuṣe suvati bhūri vāmam ||
english: The god Savitṛ who belongs to the house has stood up at the onset of dusk with golden hands; iron-jawed, adorable, sweet-tongued, he bestows great riches upon the worshipper.

sanskrit: ud ū ayām̐ upavakteva bāhū hiraṇyayā savitā supratīkā | divo rohāṁsy aruhat pṛthivyā arīramat patayat kac cid abhvam ||
english: Savitṛ of beautiful aspect has raised his golden arms up like an announcer; he has climbed the heights of heaven, of earth, he has caused whatever is enormous to fly away and made it settle.

sanskrit: vāmam adya savitar vāmam u śvo dive-dive vāmam asmabhyaṁ sāvīḥ | vāmasya hi kṣayasya deva bhūrer ayā dhiyā vāmabhājaḥ syāma ||
english: O Savitṛ, impel good fortune for us today, and also tomorrow, day by day impel good fortune for us; for, O god, with this prayer may we be partakers of great good fortune and its abode.

sanskrit: indrāsomā mahi tad vām mahitvaṁ yuvam mahāni prathamāni cakrathuḥ | yuvaṁ sūryaṁ vivididhur yuvaṁ svar viśvā tamāṁsy ahataṁ nidaś ca ||
english: O Indra-Soma, great is that greatness of you two — you two performed the great primordial deeds; you two found the sun, you two found the light, you two smote all the darknesses and the fasteners.

sanskrit: indrāsomā vāsayatha uṣāsam ut sūryaṁ nayatho jyotiṣā saha | upa dyāṁ skambhathuḥ skambhanenāprathataṁ pṛthivīm mātaraṁ vi ||
english: O Indra-Soma, you two clothe the dawn, you two lead up the sun together with his light; you two prop heaven with a prop, and you spread apart mother Earth widely.

sanskrit: indrāsomāv ahim apaḥ pariṣṭhāṁ hatho vṛtram anu vāṁ dyaur amanyata | prārṇāṁsy airayataṁ nadīnām ā samudrāṇi paprathuḥ purūṇi ||
english: O Indra-Soma, you two smote the serpent that had enclosed the waters, Vṛtra — Heaven agreed with you two in this; you two set the streams of the rivers flowing and many oceans spread wide.

sanskrit: indrāsomā pakvam āmāsv antar ni gavām id dadhathur vakṣaṇāsu | jagṛbhathur anapinaddham āsu ruśac citrāsu jagatīṣv antaḥ ||
english: O Indra-Soma, you two placed the ripe within the unripe, the essence of the cows within their flanks; you two seized that bright, shining thing inside these moving ones, it being unbound within the variegated ones.

sanskrit: indrāsomā yuvam aṅga tarutram apatyasācaṁ śrutyaṁ rarāthe | yuvaṁ śuṣmaṁ naryaṁ carṣaṇibhyaḥ saṁ vivyathuḥ pṛtanāṣāham ugrā ||
english: O Indra-Soma, you two have indeed bestowed a famous aid that accompanies the offspring; you two, fierce ones, have wrapped round the manly vigour for men, the vigour victorious in battles.

sanskrit: yo adribhit prathamajā ṛtāvā bṛhaspatir āṅgiraso haviṣmān | dvibarha jmā prāgharmasat pitā na ā rodasī vṛṣabho roravīti ||
english: He who is the rock-splitter, the first-born, the upholder of holy order, Bṛhaspati the Āṅgirasa who possesses oblations; doubly strong, having preceded the hot pressing on earth — as a father, as a bull, he roars filling Heaven and Earth.

sanskrit: janāya cid ya īvata u lokam bṛhaspatir devahūtau cakāra | ghnan vṛtrāṇi vi puro dardarīti jayañ śatrūm̐r amitrān pṛtsu sāhan ||
english: Even for a man who was seeking a dwelling-place, Bṛhaspati made a way at the invocation of the gods; smiting the Vṛtra-foes, he shatters the strongholds, conquering enemies and foes in battles, overpowering them.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiḥ sam ajayad vasūni maho vrajān gomato deva eṣaḥ | apaḥ siṣāsan svar apratīto bṛhaspatir hanty amitram arkaiḥ ||
english: Bṛhaspati won together the good things, the great cattle-pens rich in cows — this god; desiring waters and the sun, irresistible, Bṛhaspati smites the enemy with his hymns.

sanskrit: somārudrā dhārayethām asuryam pra vām iṣṭayo 'ram aśnuvantu | dame-dame sapta ratnā dadhānā śaṁ no bhūtaṁ dvipade śaṁ catuṣpade ||
english: O Soma-Rudra, uphold the divine lordly power; may the sacrificial offerings reach you two duly; bearing the seven treasures in every house — be auspicious to our two-footed, auspicious to our four-footed.

sanskrit: somārudrā vi vṛhataṁ viṣūcīm amīvā yā no gayam āviveśa | āre bādhethāṁ nirṛtim parācair asme bhadrā sauśravasāni santu ||
english: O Soma-Rudra, drive away in all directions the disease that has entered our house; drive dissolution and misfortune far away from us — may there be prosperity and great renown for us.

sanskrit: somārudrā yuvam etāny asme viśvā tanūṣu bheṣajāni dhattam | ava syatam muñcataṁ yan no asti tanūṣu baddhaṁ kṛtam eno asmat ||
english: O Soma-Rudra, place all these medicines for us in our bodies; release, loosen from us whatever sin has been committed that is bound in our bodies.

sanskrit: tigmāyudhau tigmahetī suśevau somārudrāv iha su mṛḻataṁ naḥ | pra no muñcataṁ varuṇasya pāśād gopāyataṁ naḥ sumanasyamānā ||
english: O Soma-Rudra, of sharp weapons, of sharp missiles, most benevolent — be gracious to us here; release us from Varuṇa's snare, guard us, being well-disposed toward us.

sanskrit: jīmūtasyeva bhavati pratīkaṁ yad varmī yāti samadām upasthe | anāviddhayā tanvā jaya tvaṁ sa tvā varmaṇo mahimā pipartu ||
english: His countenance becomes like a thunder-cloud when the armoured warrior goes into the lap of battles; conquer you with an unwounded body — may the greatness of the armour protect you.

sanskrit: dhanvanā gā dhanvanājiṁ jayema dhanvanā tīvrāḥ samado jayema | dhanuḥ śatror apakāmaṁ kṛṇoti dhanvanā sarvāḥ pradiśo jayema ||
english: With the bow may we win cattle, with the bow may we win battles, with the bow may we conquer the fierce conflicts; the bow renders the enemy's desire impotent — with the bow may we win all the regions.

sanskrit: vakṣyantīved ā ganīganti karṇam priyaṁ sakhāyam pariṣasvajānā | yoṣeva śiṅkte vitataādhi dhanvañ jyā iyaṁ samane pārayantī ||
english: As if about to speak, she whispers into the ear, embracing her dear friend — the bowstring stretched upon the bow twangs like a woman at the battle, carrying one across.

sanskrit: te ācarantī samaneva yoṣā māteva putram bibhṛtām upasthe | apa śatrūn vidhyatāṁ saṁvidāne ārtnī ime viṣphurantī amitrān ||
english: These two that move forward like a woman toward the battle-ground — may they, coming together, hold him on their lap as a mother holds her son; may these two bowstring-ends pierce the enemies, shooting, scattering the foes.

sanskrit: bahvīnām pitā bahur asya putraś ciścā kṛṇoti samanāvagatya | iṣudhiḥ saṅkāḥ pṛtanāś ca sarvāḥ pṛṣṭhe ninaddho jayati prasūtaḥ ||
english: Father of many, many are his sons — the quiver makes a sound when it goes down into battle; bound on the back, it conquers all conflicts and the assembled arrays when the archer is urged forward.

sanskrit: rathe tiṣṭhan nayati vājinaḥ puro yatra-yatra kāmayate suṣārathiḥ | abhīśūnām mahimānam panāyata manaḥ paścād anu yacchanti raśmayaḥ ||
english: Standing in the chariot, the skilled charioteer leads the horses forward whithersoever he desires; praise the greatness of the reins — the lines draw back the mind from behind.

sanskrit: tīvrān ghoṣān kṛṇvate vṛṣapāṇayo 'śvā rathebhiḥ saha vājayantaḥ | avakramantaḥ prapadair amitrān kṣiṇanti śatrūm̐r anapavyayantaḥ ||
english: The bull-handed horses make fierce battle-cries along with the chariots, striving for victory; stepping forward with their fore-hooves, they destroy the enemies, crushing the foes without retreat.

sanskrit: rathavāhanaṁ havir asya nāma yatrāyudhaṁ nihitam asya varma | tatrā ratham upa śagmaṁ sadema viśvāhā vayaṁ sumanasyamānāḥ ||
english: The chariot's burden — that is its name, the oblation — where the weapon is laid, where its armour is; there may we be seated beside the mighty chariot, always well-disposed.

sanskrit: svāduṣaṁsadaḥ pitaro vayodhāḥ kṛcchreśritaḥ śaktīvanto gabhīrāḥ | citrasenā iṣubalā amṛdhrāḥ satovīrā uravo vrātasāhāḥ ||
english: Sweet to sit with, fathers, strength-givers, having taken refuge in hardship, powerful and deep; with brilliant armies, mighty in arrows, unyielding, rich in real heroes, broad, overcoming hosts.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāsaḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ śive no dyāvāpṛthivī anehasā | pūṣā naḥ pātu duritād ṛtāvṛdho rakṣā mākin no aghaśaṁsa īśata ||
english: Brāhmaṇas, fathers, Soma-drinkers — may Heaven and Earth be auspicious and unharming to us; may Pūṣan, increaser of holy order, guard us from evil — may no evil-speaker have power over us.

sanskrit: suparṇaṁ vaste mṛgo asyā danto gobhiḥ saṁnaddhā patati prasūtā | yatrā naraḥ saṁ ca vi ca dravanti tatrāsmabhyam iṣavaḥ śarma yaṁsan ||
english: A bird's feather clothes it, the animal's tooth is hers — bound with cow's sinew she flies when launched; where men run together and apart, there may the arrows grant shelter to us.

sanskrit: ṛjīte pari vṛṅdhi no 'śmā bhavatu nas tanūḥ | somo adhi bravītu no 'ditiḥ śarma yacchatu ||
english: O Arrow, ward off from us; may our body become stone; may Soma speak for us, may Aditi grant us shelter.

sanskrit: ā jaṅghanti sānv eṣāṁ jaghanām̐ upa jighnate | aśvājani pracetaso 'śvān samatsu codaya ||
english: She strikes against their backs, touches their hindquarters — O horse-whip of the discerning one, urge the horses forward in the battles.

sanskrit: ahir iva bhogaiḥ pary eti bāhuṁ jyāyā hetim paribādhamānaḥ | hastaghno viśvā vayunāni vidvān pumān pumāṁsam pari pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: Like a serpent with its coils it winds around the arm, the bowstring repelling the dart; the arm-guard knowing all the ways of motion — may this man guard that man on all sides.

sanskrit: ālāktā yā ruruśīrṣṇy atho yasyā ayo mukham | idam parjanyaretasa iṣvai devyai bṛhan namaḥ ||
english: She that is painted red, with the head of the roebuck, and whose mouth is of iron — to this divine arrow, born of the seed of Parjanya, great homage.

sanskrit: avasṛṣṭā parā pata śaravye brahmasaṁśite | gacchāmitrān pra padyasva māmīṣāṁ kaṁ canocci śiṣaḥ ||
english: Released, fly forth, O shaft, sharpened by Brahman prayer; fly to the enemies, strike among them — do not leave any one of these alive.

sanskrit: yatra bāṇāḥ sampatanti kumārā viśikhā iva | tatrā no brahmaṇas patir aditiḥ śarma yacchatu viśvāhā śarma yacchatu ||
english: Where the arrows fly together like boys with unbound hair — there may Brahmaṇaspati grant us shelter, may Aditi grant us shelter, grant us shelter always.

sanskrit: marmāṇi te varmaṇā chādayāmi somas tvā rājāmṛtenānu vastām | uro varīyo varuṇas te kṛṇotu jayantaṁ tvānu devā madantu ||
english: I cover your vital spots with armour; may King Soma clothe you about with immortality; may Varuṇa make broad space for you, broad and wider still — may the gods rejoice following you as you conquer.

sanskrit: yo naḥ svo araṇo yaś ca niṣṭyo jighāṁsati | devās taṁ sarve dhūrvantu brahma varma mamāntaram ||
english: He who desires to slay us, whether one of our own or a stranger — may all the gods confound him; the sacred prayer is my innermost armour.
